title: A long edit with transitions plays, scrubs and edits without a stutter: measure it, then make it fast
goal: With a moderately complex 6 minute video with transitions, performance tanked: playback, scrubbing and editing all slowed. Build a reference edit and a perf harness that measures it the way a person uses it, find where the time goes, and fix the biggest costs until playback, scrubbing and editing meet the video-perf objective's numbers. Then file the remaining costs as follow-up tasks under video-perf, each with its own measured bar.
notes: User, 2026-11-12 (intake): 'With a moderately complex 6minute video with transitions, perf tanked. I think we need to focus on perf so that editing and playing back video is top notch and scalable.' video-perf was made the objectives focus the same day, with its success numbers. Existing pieces to read first: Sources/PhotonzCore/MoviePlayPass.swift, PlaybackKeepsUp.swift, the scrubbing task scrubbing-is-smooth-never-goes-black-and-the-pic. Runs are long: keep each runner pass inside the three passes a day cap by splitting into the follow-ups above.
acceptance: A reference edit generator kept in the repo (Scripts/perf/) that builds a 6 minute document from real screen recordings: 3 or more tracks, 30 or more cuts with dissolves, a push and a 3D transition, titles, zooms, a moving background, attached sound; and 20 and 60 minute versions. Deterministic, so every run measures the same thing.

A perf harness (a walk or a probe script) that plays the whole edit at 1x, scrubs end to end, and trims, moves, blades and undoes while playing, recording: dropped frames and the worst frame time during playback, frame latency while scrubbing, the longest main thread pass per edit, memory over time, and export time. Its numbers go in the audit before any fix.

Profile with Instruments (Time Profiler, the Metal and Core Animation templates) on the reference edit and say in the audit where the time goes, ranked: decoding, compositing transitions, the timeline's SwiftUI updates, waveform and thumbnail drawing, the main thread, memory churn.

Fix the biggest costs in this task (likely candidates to confirm, not assume: decoding ahead of the playhead, caching composited transition frames, timeline views redrawing for every frame, per-frame allocations) until, on the 6 minute edit: 1x playback drops no frames, scrubbing shows the frame under the pointer within one display frame, and each edit finishes within 16 ms on the main thread. Each fix with a before and after number.

What is not reached here is filed as follow-up tasks under video-perf (p1, source user), one cost each, with its measured bar and the harness command that checks it. The 20 and 60 minute versions are measured and their numbers recorded even if not yet fixed.

No change in what is drawn: export of the reference edit is byte for byte the same before and after (or within a stated tolerance, measured). Perf note in every commit that touches the composite path.

Once the per-tick SwiftUI cost is found, the rule it implies (which views may watch the playhead on every tick, and how the rest read it) is written into the video design notes in docs/design, so the next view added to the window does not slow playback again. Two of the four fixes so far were this same pattern: work recomputed per query (track layout) and views re-reading the playhead (timeline menus).
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: manager pass 2026-11-12: split so each runner sitting finishes. The reference edit (first acceptance line) is a-long-reference-edit-opens-in-the-probe-in-one; the speed walk, baseline and ranked profile (second and third lines) are a-speed-walk-measures-the-long-reference-edit-th. Both are deps of this task, so it starts from their baseline and ranked list and does the fixes (lines four to six). The timeline at hundreds of clips, export time and memory each have their own task under video-perf.

Acceptance line 1 (the reference edit generator) is done by a-long-reference-edit-opens-in-the-probe-in-one: Sources/PhotonzCore/ReferenceEdit.swift (layout, seeded), Sources/PhotonzMedia/ReferenceFootage.swift (Retina 60 fps recordings, voice, music, kept per machine), Scripts/perf/reference-edit.sh 6|20|60, walk setup referenceEdit. Reproduced the complaint on it: at 1x the picture fell up to 124 frames behind the playhead and the main thread froze for up to 4.3 s per pass on the 6 minute edit. Model costs seen while building it at 60 minutes: PhotonzDocument.land ~40 ms per clip and setTransition(at: .edit) ~100 ms per cut, because track layout and edit points are recomputed per call. Opening long edits filed as an-hour-long-edit-opens-in-a-few-seconds-not-two.

From the speed walk (a-speed-walk-measures-the-long-reference-edit-th, 2026-11-12): the ranked list for this slice. Main thread 100% busy while the 6 minute edit plays; about 95% of it is edit point and track arithmetic that rebuilds PhotonzDocument.trackLayout() on every query: MoviePlayLookahead.points per tick (68%), editPointCut/editPointMoments elsewhere (15%), withEditPointTransitionsDrawn per picture (9%), editPointSoundCrossings (4%), isCutLocked in the timeline (3%); 44% of leaf time is copying Layers. Decoding and compositing are not it (7 to 54 ms a picture, off the main thread, but only ~10 pictures asked for a minute). Result: 5 of ~1850 frames shown in a minute of play, worst gap 17 to 28 s. Judge the fix with Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh (short) and --long; write the new baseline into Scripts/perf/baselines/short-6.json when it gets faster. Also seen: a blade (B) while playing stops playback (splitClipAtPlayhead calls pauseDocument); Premiere's Add Edit and Final Cut's Blade keep playing.

Fix 1: the document keeps its track layout, edit points and edit-point transitions until its layers/tracks/duration change (Sources/PhotonzCore/DocumentDerived.swift, didSets in Document.swift). Unit: one playing tick on the 6 min edit 2,100 ms -> 2.6 ms (debug, PlayTickPerfTests). Short speed walk: 4/1857 -> 934/1819 frames shown, worst gap 17.9 s -> 183 ms, scrub lag median 160 -> 20 refreshes, trim 5.7 s -> 90 ms, blade 1.4 s -> 169 ms, undo 4.0 s -> 110 ms. Next: Time Profiler shows the main thread still ~87% SwiftUI updates, mostly every edit point's view rebuilding its right-click menu each tick (rows read the playhead); and the clock sleeps 33 ms AFTER each tick's work.

Landed (c771adfbb, 0582a551c, 8f1d0bc46): (1) the document keeps its track layout, edit points and edit-point transitions (DocumentDerived.swift); (2) timeline right-click menus read the playhead unwatched and rebuild on each right click (EditorState.timelineMenuRows); (3) the playing clock keeps its own 33 ms beat (PlayClockPace); (4) a scrub could hang the whole app once (1) made it fast: blocking movie reads filled Swift's cooperative pool; now at most half the cores' worth read at once (MovieSweeper.gate). Drawn output proven unchanged (digest of 362 moments + frame requests + mix identical before/after). Short walk baseline rewritten (worst of 3), margin tightened 100% -> 50%. Audit: queue/audits/2026-11-13-a-long-edit-with-transitions-plays-scrubs-and-ed.json.

Reached vs bar on the 6 min edit: playback 1440-1551 of ~1819 frames in a minute (bar: none dropped), worst gap 118-128 ms; scrub 8 / 19 display frames behind (bar: 1); edits while playing trim 90, blade 203, undo 119 ms (bar: 16). 20 and 60 min measured (in the audit). Left: Time Profiler says ~86% of the main thread playing is SwiftUI graph work after each playhead move (ObservationGraphMutation ~15%, AccessibilityViewGraph 8-12%, few bodies rebuilt): find what high in the window is dirtied per tick. Judge with Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh; profile with xctrace + Scripts/perf/rank-trace.py. Gotcha: attaching Time Profiler to the short walk can push it past its 300 s clock.

Left rough, not filed: B (blade) while playing still stops playback where Premiere's Add Edit keeps playing; a behaviour change, already asked of the user in the speed walk audit's evaluate list. Roll Edit's title in a cut's right-click menu now names the playhead as it was at the right click rather than live. Memory regression on the 60 min edit folded into memory-stays-bounded-while-an-hour-long-edit-pla; SwiftUI per-tick cost folded into the-timeline-of-an-hour-long-edit-scrolls-zooms.

Four fixes landed: playback 4 -> ~1450 of 1819 frames a minute, worst gap 17.9 s -> 125 ms, scrub lag 160 -> 8 frames, edits 1.4-5.7 s -> 90-203 ms on the 6 min edit. Bars (no dropped frames, scrub within 1 frame, edits <=16 ms) not yet reached: the remaining cost is SwiftUI graph work per playhead move.

triage 2026-11-13: added an acceptance line asking for the playhead-watching rule to be written down once found. Recurring pattern across this task, the speed walk and the open-time bug: derived data rebuilt on every query and views that watch the playhead every tick.

Pass 2 found the per-tick SwiftUI cost: every SwiftUI pass over the window costs about as much again as the timeline's tracks have views, whatever starts it (20 s play: 500/606 shipped, 605/606 with only the tracks hidden; no clip/track/row body runs per tick). So fewer passes per frame: (5) panel Time section + cut facts watch PanelPlayhead not the playhead (EditorState+PanelPlayhead.swift), 495 -> 576; (6) canvas reads the playhead unwatched via a closure; (7) playing/scrubbed frames go straight onto the canvas layer (EditorState.showPlayingPicture / CanvasNSView.showPlayingPicture), 576 -> 603. Also refreshCrispTile no longer writes nil over nil. Commit 6b216a785; rule written in docs/design/video.md 8f (acceptance line 7). Short-walk baseline rewritten: dropped 379 -> 6-10 a minute, transitions 0-1 dropped, scrub 7/21 (was 8/19), edits trim 85 blade 225 undo 127 ms.

Reached vs bar after pass 2 (6 min edit): playback 6-10 of 1818 frames dropped a minute (bar: none), worst gap 105-130 ms; scrub 6-8 display frames behind median, 20-21 worst (bar: 1), barely moved, so its time is in reading frames, not SwiftUI; edits while playing 80-230 ms (bar: 16), each edit rebuilds the whole timeline. Next: (a) the frame fast path steps aside when something is picked, so play with a clip picked still makes a SwiftUI pass per frame; (b) profile the scrub: decode latency per seek; (c) edits: an edit rebuilds every track row, so make rows depend on their own clips only. Tools that worked: per-body counters inserted temporarily, A/B hiding of regions behind a file flag, and an lldb auto-continue breakpoint on ObservationRegistrar.withMutation to list per-tick observed writes. The xctrace SwiftUI template on a launched probe produced an 8 GB trace that never finished saving: do not use it.
